brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. The five quarter cameras were framed when the town was smaller and they now frame GROUND, not the town. Two measurements, both re-runnable on HEAD before you build anything: (1) probes/world-edge-framing.mjs — the world's east face, where #119 hung a gate open in a hedge, is off-canvas in every camera but Wide at desktop sizes including the quarter NAMED 'Far bank', and off-frame in all five on a phone; viewFor's held() clamps ox inside x=0..GW and drawFieldEdge paints PAST GW. (2) c150 — no quarter reaches s > 1.02 on the clock tower so the vanes' cardinals never leave their 6 px floor, 'Far bank' holds no sky above the tower, and 'Courtyard' shows void west of x=0. Teach viewFor the world it actually has: an extent the ground cache paints rather than the grid's 0..GW, and a per-quarter vertical INTENT, so a quarter whose subject is tall (the church tower and its vane, the murmuration, the roofline) gets the air its subject stands in instead of being fitted to a ground box. The frame is the picture above sillTop(); q.share still sets s from WIDTH alone, which is the seam LAWS already names.
successLooksLike: Cycling #where at 1600x950 and at 390x844, each of the five frames contains the thing it is named after, in full: Far bank shows the hedge, the open gate and the track, and sky above the clock tower; Courtyard shows no void past the west wall; at least one quarter zooms far enough that a vane's cardinal letters are legible. No quarter shows void off any edge. Wide is hash-identical to HEAD at pinned instants — the wide shot is the control, and it must not move.
avoid: Do not add a sixth quarter — the five that exist are the problem, not the count. Do not move any world geometry to suit a frame. Do not touch FOCUS: the ground-cache ease depends on it being fixed, and a moved FOCUS makes every quarter a cache repaint. And do not 'fix' a quarter by zooming out — a quarter that shows everything is the Wide shot again.
